source_text: Μαρτυρεῖ δὲ ὁ μακάριος Πολύκαρπος μηνὸς Ξανθικοῦ δευτέρᾳ ἱσταμένου, πρὸ ἑπτὰ καλανδῶν Μαρτίων, σαββάτῳ μεγάλῳ, ὥρᾳ ὀγδόῃ. συνελήφθη δὲ ὑπὸ Ἡρώδου ἐπὶ ἀρχιερέως Φιλίππου Τραλλιανοῦ, ἀνθυπατεύοντος Στατίου Κοδράτου, βασιλεύοντος δὲ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: ᾧ ἡ δόξα, τιμή, μεγαλωσύνη, θρόνος αἰώνιος ἀπὸ γενεᾶς εἰς γενεάν. ἀμήν.
orientation: The church of Smyrna closes its letter by recording the precise date and circumstances of Polycarp's arrest and martyrdom.
pass_a_gloss: And the blessed Polycarp bore witness [as a martyr] on the second [day] of the beginning month Xanthicus, seven [days] before the kalends of March, on a great Sabbath, at the eighth hour. And he was arrested by Herod, when Philip of Tralles was high priest, when Statius Quadratus was proconsul, and when Jesus Christ was reigning forever: to whom [be] the glory, honor, greatness, eternal throne from generation to generation. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'martyr' for μάρτυς; here the verb μαρτυρέω in this context means to die as a martyr, so 'was martyred' keeps the glossary sense while fitting the historical statement.

choices.english: on the second day of the beginning of the month
choices.why: ἱσταμένου is a technical term for the first part of the month in Greek dating; rendering it as 'beginning' preserves the calendrical precision.
rejected: on the second of the month
on the second day from the start

choices.english: seven days before the kalends of March
choices.why: This is the standard Roman dating formula; keeping 'kalends' as a technical term preserves the Roman calendar reference.
rejected: seven days before the first of March
on the seventh day before the March kalends

choices.why: The glossary fixes ἀνθύπατος as 'proconsul'; the participle form is rendered with 'while' to show the temporal circumstance.
rejected: under the proconsulship of Statius Quadratus

choices.term: βασιλεύοντος δὲ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
choices.english: and while Jesus Christ reigns forever
choices.why: The contrast between the earthly officials and Christ's eternal reign is the point; 'forever' captures εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας idiomatically.
rejected: and Jesus Christ being king forever
and with Jesus Christ ruling unto the ages

choices.why: The doxology ascribes an eternal throne to Christ; 'eternal' is the natural English for αἰώνιος here.

pass_b_english: The blessed Polycarp was martyred on the second day of the month Xanthicus, seven days before the first of March, on the great Sabbath, at the eighth hour. He was arrested by Herod, the police captain, while Philip of Tralles was high priest and Statius Quadratus was proconsul, and while Jesus Christ reigns forever. To him be glory, honor, greatness, and an eternal throne from generation to generation. Amen.

polish.changed: Clarified Herod's title, simplified the calendar reference, and smoothed the sentence flow while preserving all details.

notes.quote: the second day of the beginning of the month Xanthicus
notes.why: Xanthicus is an obscure ancient month unknown to modern readers.
notes.fix: Explain: “Xanthicus, the first month of the Macedonian calendar (roughly March).”

notes.quote: seven days before the kalends of March
notes.why: The Roman term “kalends” is not defined.
notes.fix: Add a note: “the Kalends of March = the first day of March in the Roman calendar.”

variants.text: the father of the police captain Herod

notes.why: Herod's title appears as 'police captain' in sections 6, 8, 17 but bare name in 21; reader may not connect.

notes.quote: the second day of the beginning of the month Xanthicus, seven days before the kalends of March
notes.why: Complex Macedonian/Roman calendar conversion; reader cannot parse date.

notes.quote: Philip of Tralles was high priest
notes.why: Unexplained civic/religious office in Asian imperial cult.
notes.fix: Note: 'high priest of the imperial cult in the province of Asia.'

polish.changed: Clarified that Herod is the police captain and Statius Quadratus is the proconsul, so the two Roman authorities are distinct; kept the ancient month name Xanthicus as in the source.

notes.why: Same Roman authority is called both “proconsul” and “police captain”.
Name of the proconsul is given without context.
notes.fix: Add a note that he was the Roman proconsul of Asia at the time.

notes.why: Xanthicus is an ancient month name unfamiliar to modern readers.
notes.fix: State that Xanthicus corresponds to a month in the Macedonian calendar (roughly November).
